howToSteps.name: Spoon it into the cup
howToSteps.text: Spoon the cocoa into the measuring cup until it heaps over the top. Do not scoop with the cup itself. Scooping packs the light powder down.

howToSteps.name: Level it off
howToSteps.text: Sweep the flat edge of a knife across the rim of the cup, back into the bag. The cup is now level and holds one cup, 84 grams.

howToSteps.name: Sift before using
howToSteps.text: Tip the measured cocoa into a fine sieve and sift it into the bowl. This breaks up the clumps so the cocoa mixes evenly into the batter.

howToSteps.name: Convert or weigh
howToSteps.text: Weigh the cocoa if you have a scale: one level cup should read 84 grams. Or use the converter above. Cups times 84 is grams, grams divided by 84 is cups.

name: Cocoa Powder
sourceNote: King Arthur Baking lists unsweetened cocoa at 42 g per 1/2 cup, so 1 cup is 84 g.
title: Cocoa Powder Cups to Grams Converter
tutorial: Cocoa powder is light. A cup of it weighs just 84 grams. Less than a cup of flour, and a quarter of what a cup of honey weighs. It is ground fine and full of air, which is why a scoop of cocoa feels like almost nothing in your hand.

The number comes from King Arthur Baking's chart: 42 grams per half cup, so a full cup is 84 grams. Measure it spooned and levelled, the same way as flour. Spoon it into the cup, level it off with a knife. Scooping packs it down and you end up with more cocoa than the recipe wants. Too much cocoa makes a cake bitter.

Cocoa clumps. The fine powder picks up moisture from the air and forms little hard balls that do not dissolve in batter. Sift it before you use it, every time, especially for frosting and hot chocolate. Sifting takes ten seconds and saves a lumpy cake.

Use the converter in either direction. Cups become grams for the scale, grams become cups when you are working without one. The anchors are easy: half a cup is 42 grams, a quarter cup is 21 grams. Most chocolate cakes call for somewhere between those two numbers.

One thing worth knowing: Dutch-process cocoa and natural cocoa weigh the same per cup. They taste different and they react differently with baking soda, but a cup of either one is 84 grams. Swap them by weight, never by guessing.
